name: NY Steak with Tomato-Basil Compound Butter, Asparagus & Loaded Baked Potato (Two Ways)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe was created to feed two adults and two young children. You know your child (their tastes and appetite) best. Use this recipe as a template, adjusting ingredients, cooking methods, and portions as needed.
Small dice butter, place in a small bowl, and set aside to soften.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 medium russet potatoes
¼ small pkg fresh basil
1 ½ small bunch asparagus

instructions.primary_message: Wash and dry potatoes. Prick all over with a fork, then transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake until potatoes are tender, so a knife can easily pierce through the flesh, about 1 hour. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, medium dice bacon.

Once the skillet is hot, add bacon and cook, stirring occasionally, until crispy, 3-4 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, remove crispy bacon to a paper towel-lined plate; set aside. (Reserve skillet with drippings for later use.)
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, pick basil leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the butter.
Peel and mince garlic. Drain and mince sun-dried tomatoes. Add both to the bowl, along with spices, then mash with the back of a spoon to combine the compound butter. Set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 clove garlic
2 sun-dried tomatoes, oil-packed
¼ tsp salt
⅛ tsp crushed red pepper
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: When the potatoes have about 15 minutes left, preheat another skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
instructions.secondary_message:
454 g striploin (New York strip) steak
½ tsp salt
¼ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom; add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and set aside to rest, 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, snap (or cut) off woody ends of the asparagus; cut spears into 1-inch long pieces.
Return the skillet with bacon drippings to medium-high heat. Once hot, add asparagus, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until tender-crisp, 4-5 minutes. Remove from heat.
instructions.secondary_message:
¼ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Cut about one-third of the steak into bite-sized pieces and set aside for the kid plates. Thinly slice remaining steak and set aside.
Cut one potato into bite-sized pieces. Split remaining potatoes lengthwise down the center.

FOR THE KID PLATES: Divide a ⅔-cup of asparagus, diced steak, and potato pieces between plates. Serve with a dollop of sour cream, a small pile of bacon, and cheese (if desired). FOR THE ADULT PLATES: Divide remaining asparagus, sliced steak, and split potatoes between plates. Top steak with compound butter and baked potato with remaining sour cream, bacon, and cheese. Enjoy!
instructions.secondary_message:
⅓ cup sour cream
⅓ cup cheddar cheese, shredded
